meta: Base 889c13f (main) → branch improve/20261012-1644, PR #121 · 2026-10-12 16:44–20:45Z · headless Chromium 141, SwiftShader, 4 vCPU · every timing is an interleaved A/B (each pair base and head run back to back); a change is called only when every pair agrees and it beats 5% and the pairs’ spread.

items.title: Review and merge PR #121
items.body:
The warm-up of the marks of play draws in one frame instead of thirteen (−11 lines), three correctness fixes (a computer that could stall for ever, a computer game that rewound after its storage filled, guessable game ids), and seven checks that could pass on broken code, or rules nothing enforced, now enforced. No primary row is faster beyond noise; the run’s speed change for a player (below) is held back for your call. On the final commit against main, the primary rows run at ×1.106 (3 pairs), none called worse, one called better (the start page’s first click −39%, a path the branch does not touch). The run’s rule is never more than 3% slower, and five primary rows lean past it without a call: the computer’s first frame +9.1% (1.11 1.14 1.02), a shared game’s page +8.4%, reopening +8.1%, selecting +5.4% (1.10 1.10 0.96), the phone start page +3.6% (all pairs slower). The shared page, reopen and the start page run no code the branch changed (their −21%, −0.5% and −0.7% in the 4-pair A/B on f6e8215 show the VM’s swing); the computer’s first frame and selecting do run the one-frame warm-up (924cb6f), and selecting leaned slower in all three of WF’s A/Bs (+12%, +2.7%, +5.4%). Not settled within the run’s budget. CI green on 50bc357; the head after it (d48eb00) changes only bench/loop/.

It bundles a server change (SystemRandom ids, one server test), bench and lint changes with the client work; CLAUDE.md asks for one logical change per PR.

items.title: Keep the one-frame warm-up although selection leans slower?
items.body: The one-frame warm-up (924cb6f) removes 11 lines and twelve whole-scene frames; the first pick leaned faster (7 of 8 pairs). The primary “Selecting a piece” row (median of 8 picks) leaned slower in each of its three A/Bs: +12%, +2.7%, +5.4%, none called, with pairs ranging 0.52–1.95. The run’s rule is never more than 3% slower; the evidence neither clears it nor shows a cost. A mechanism for a slower median is not obvious (the warm-up ends sooner, not later), but I did not prove there is none.

items.title: The first-pick fix moves the warm-up’s cost rather than removing it: take it anyway? (reverted, patch kept)
items.body: In software rendering the warm-up of the marks of play costs about 2 s of GPU time, and it lands on whatever the player does first after the entrance: on main, the first pick (about 2.4 s). W1b linked those programs under the entrance and read them back once the board rested. The first pick dropped to 0.8–1.05 s (called better in three A/Bs), but the second and third picks and the computer’s second reply each waited about 0.3 s more, and the primary “Selecting a piece” row (the median of 8 picks) leaned slower twice on the final code: +41% (0.95 1.58 1.43 1.85) and +37% (1.02 1.95 1.29), neither called. The run’s rule is never more than 3% slower, and CLAUDE.md calls buying one wait with another a trade-off, not a win, so I reverted it (20bb91f, 50bc357). It is in bench/loop/patches/warm-under-entrance-W1b.patch.

items.title: The join’s wait: fewer lobby frames while the board links? (design call)
items.body: A CPU profile of a join shows the joiner’s long tasks are getUniforms read-backs inside render(), each waiting for the GPU to finish the lobby frames queued before it (0.66, 1.15, 0.53 s), plus 0.3 s creating the board’s WebGL context. Linking ahead (tried, rejected) moves links, not those waits. What would shorten them is drawing fewer lobby frames while the board’s canvas starts: the arrival’s ring and lift would step instead of glide in software.

items.title: The 1.2× target against the first recorded run is not met
items.body: The target was the primary rows 1.2× faster than the first recorded run (92ce041). Measured today on e4ee30c (before W1b’s revert; its first-pick and selection rows include W1b), 3 pairs (92ce041 had no computer player, so those two rows are missing): ×0.893 (last run measured ×0.968 on its own code; the two runs’ VMs differ, so compare within a run only). Called better: a shared game’s page −44%, reopening a long game −31%. Called worse: joining’s first board frame 1.57 → 5.12 s (+216%), the opponent’s move landing 136 → 215 ms (+58%; against main this run it was −5.8%, not called, so it came in before this branch; it was +4.6% uncalled last run), the phone start page +7.4%. Still worse in the diagnostics: the first pick 33 ms → 764 ms (2.34 s last run), JS heap on a reopened 2,000-ply game +34%, one texture more after 16 plies (the garden copy, not a leak: X5a). The lobby, the garden, the preview and the entrance all came after 92ce041; the join remains the largest wait.

items.title: Rows that leaned slower without being called
items.body: On the final commit (3 pairs), one diagnostic was called worse: create → share link shown +27% (1.39 1.16 1.28; +22% leaning in the 4-pair A/B on f6e8215). No code on that path changed on the branch (the lobby, the socket and the side choice are untouched; the warm-up runs on a board only), and the row has two modes (ledger B1/L1), so I read it as the VM; it is the first thing to recheck. Primary rows leaning slower without a call are listed under Needs from me. In the earlier A/Bs: reopen long tasks total +18% and the phone’s click → side choice +30% leaned slower on f6e8215 (+6.7% and not repeated on later runs). Also on the final commit, leaning slower without a call: the phone’s main-thread script to ready +9.4% (1.25 1.04 1.01), the phone’s longest task +7.1% (1.19 1.02 1.02), the joiner’s long tasks total +15%; none on a path the branch changed except through the warm-up, which runs on a board only.

items.title: Three silent failures fixed
items.body:
• The computer stalled for ever, saying nothing, if its search chose a move the rules refuse (its board and the engine disagreeing). It now logs the move and plays on (8b968ce).
  • A computer game that outgrew storage rewound to the last copy storage took on a remount or a reload; it now plays on from its latest move, and says so once in the console (5317469).
  • Game ids, the whole credential for an open seat, came from Python’s Mersenne Twister; now from the system’s entropy (26bae12).

items.title: Checks that could pass on broken code, and rules nothing enforced
items.body:
• The computer’s primary row timed a fixed node count: a search made weaker would read faster. It now pins depth, move and the nodes to finish that depth; removing the killer/history updates kept depth and move and now fails on nodes (12,099 → 17,999) (df8083c).
  • The A/B never called a “longest task” row that goes 0 → N ms (a move that starts to hold the page); now it does, and only then (8a020e8, 1aa90ee after review).
  • The server’s “replaced socket” test checked before the disconnect was processed (3016c9b); hudFit passed with nothing measured (e5759d9); the bench’s wait for a pick’s destinations never waited (8311a5b).
  • Lint now stops a board set outside the engine, animation on the browser’s frames or the wall clock, and two ways round the schema and __r3fState rules (a446a69, c023ab5); the build fails if the tutorial’s or a computer game’s page lands in the start page’s bytes (ab48319). Each was planted and seen to fail.
  • One table for the history’s keys, its titles and a new aria-keyshortcuts (f6e8215).

Nothing deleted outright: pointerEvents.ts (−44, N4′) needs a browser check that competes with timings and was left open. Not kept: LW (+60) and W1b (+29), patches in bench/loop/patches/.

items.title: Smaller
items.body:
• React 19.3: +15.8 KB gz on react-dom, nothing a player waits on faster (measured on the tarballs by a reviewer).
  • Replacing the bench’s PIECE_PIXEL with squarePixel: it rounds to whole pixels and re-casts, which the other does not.

choices.intro:
• Reverted W1b myself (it broke the run’s 3% rule on the primary selection row), rather than leaving it in for you to judge; the patch is one apply away.
  • A refused computer save is logged, not shown: a line on screen is new interface copy (CLAUDE.md), so it is yours to decide (ledger R5).
  • The computer’s fallback for a refused search move is its first legal move, logged, not a new search without that move (R3 open).
  • Merged lenses 1 and 10 into one reviewer; React 19.3 left out (+15.8 KB gz, nothing faster).
  • Kept PIECE_PIXEL in the bench (it rounds to whole pixels; the duplicate does not).
  • Bundled server, bench and lint changes with the client work in one PR, as the last runs did; the recommendation is to split (Needs from me).

notConfirmed.intro:
• The A/B against the first recorded run (×0.893) ran on e4ee30c, before W1b’s revert; not rechecked on the final commit 50bc357.
  • Whether the five primary rows leaning slower on the final commit (above) are noise: 3 pairs could not settle them, and no A/A spread was taken this run.
  • No row measures the entrance’s or the handover’s frame gaps (T16); the showcase records on a virtual clock. W1b would have moved GPU work under both; it is reverted.
  • The move-latency timeouts in the W1b A/B (once per side): not seen again in the later A/Bs.
  • N4′ (remove pointerEvents.ts): needs leaving / and /learn at once in a browser; not run.
  • React 19.3’s size (+15.8 KB gz) was measured by a reviewer on the npm tarballs, not by a build here.

merge.intro:
No other sessions were active. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or ARCHITECTURE.md needed changing for this diff (the warm-up’s draw schedule is described only in warm.tsx). Proposed for shared files, not installed:

  • .claude/hooks/format.sh: add "$root"/client/scripts/*.mjs|"$root"/client/*.html|"$root"/bench/*.mjs to its prettier case; the lint checks them and the hook does not format them (E8).
  • server/pyproject.toml: add pytest-timeout (e.g. 30 s); a socket regression in the server tests hangs instead of failing (R8).
  • CLAUDE.md: a short North star (what the game is for, what it is not). This run, like the last five, used “Performance”, bench/loop/ and the test suites in place of the loop prompt’s North star, Measurement, Reporting, Loop state and Tests sections.
